Operating Characteristics of the TITE-gBOIN-ET Design in Several Scenarios

Source: R/sim_tite_gboin_et_multi.R
sim_tite_gboin_et_multi.Rd

Run sim_tite_gboin_et for several scenarios of probabilities of toxicity and efficacy categories with the same design, and collect the results in one table.

Usage

sim_tite_gboin_et_multi(
  target,
  target_resp,
  scenarios,
  score,
  score_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  window,
  accrual_rate,
  resp_window = window,
  accrual = c("uniform", "exponential", "fixed"),
  event_time = c("weibull", "uniform"),
  late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  min_completed_share = 0.5,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  lambda1 = NULL,
  lambda2 = NULL,
  eta1 = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  est_method = c("observed", "fp_linear", "fp_logistic"),
  obd_method = c("max_resp", "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear",
    "utility_scoring"),
  min_obd_sample = 1,
  w1 = 0.33,
  w2 = 1.09,
  t_low = NULL,
  t_upp = NULL,
  e_low = NULL,
  e_upp = NULL,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.47 / 1.5 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized efficacy score, for example 0.95 / 1.5 for a target equivalent efficacy score of 0.95 with a largest score of 1.5.

scenarios

A list of scenarios, each a list with the components p_grade and p_resp_grade, matrices as the arguments of the same names of sim_gboin_et, and optionally name. The names of the list are used as scenario names. Every scenario must have the same numbers of categories and of doses.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

score_resp

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_resp_grade. Score of each efficacy category, for example c(0, 1, 1.5) for stable or progressive disease, partial response and complete response. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

window

Numeric scalar. Length of the toxicity assessment window.

accrual_rate

Numeric scalar. Average number of patients arriving per unit of time, in the same unit as window. The accrual argument of the 'boinet' package is the average time between arrivals, its inverse.

resp_window

Numeric scalar. Length of the efficacy assessment window. Defaults to window.

accrual

Character scalar. Distribution of the times between arrivals: "uniform" (the default, as in 'boinet') on (0, 2 / accrual_rate), "exponential" for a Poisson process, or "fixed" for arrivals exactly 1 / accrual_rate apart.

event_time

Character scalar. Distribution of the times to the toxicity event and to the efficacy event: "weibull" (the default), with the share of the events in the second half of the window set by late_fraction and resp_late_fraction, or "uniform" on (0, window / p) for an event of probability p. With "weibull" the first category of both outcomes, the one without an event, must have a positive probability at every dose.

late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Share of the toxicity events that occur in the second half of the toxicity window under the Weibull distribution. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. The same for the efficacy events. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the time to the toxicity event and the time to the efficacy event of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

min_completed_share

Numeric scalar from 0 to 1. Share of the patients at the current dose who must have finished both assessments before the next decision; the decision waits until then. Defaults to 0.5, the rule of Takeda et al. (2023) and of the 'boinet' package.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at any dose. Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size, which is the default of the 'boinet' package.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

Numeric scalars or NULL. Boundaries of the mean toxicity score and of the mean efficacy score. Defaults to NULL, the boundaries of boin_et_boundary for the targets. Give all three to use other values, such as those printed in an article.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly. Defaults to FALSE, which keeps to Takeda et al. (2018), who do not allow dose skipping during escalation; see Details.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimator of the mean efficacy scores: "observed" (the default) for the observed means, "fp_linear" for the linear fractional polynomial of Takeda et al. (2022), or "fp_logistic" for the fractional polynomial logistic regression of the 'boinet' package, which needs the 'mfp' package.

obd_method

Character scalar. Selection rule: "max_resp" (the default) for the admissible dose with the highest estimated response rate up to the estimated MTD, or the dose that maximizes the utility "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear" or "utility_scoring" among the admissible doses.

min_obd_sample

Integer scalar. Only doses given to at least this many patients can be selected. Defaults to 1. The simulations of Takeda et al. (2022) use 6.

w1, w2

Numeric scalars. Weights of the weighted utility q - w1 * p - w2 * p * (p > p_tox), where p and q are the estimated DLT and response rates. Default to 0.33 and 1.09.

t_low, t_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. DLT rates between which the truncated linear utility falls from one to zero. Default to p_saf and p_tox.

e_low, e_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. Response rates between which the truncated linear utility rises from zero to one. Default to p_saf_resp / 2 and target_resp.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of the scoring utility for a patient with neither DLT nor response and for a patient with both, the scores of a response without DLT and of a DLT without response being 100 and 0. Default to 40 and 60.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials and the selected OBDs in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress with messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_et_oc_multi, as returned by sim_gboin_et_multi, whose results are the boin_et_oc objects of sim_tite_gboin_et.

Details

Every scenario is simulated with the same seed, as in sim_boin_et_multi.

References

Takeda, K., Yamaguchi, Y., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2023). TITE-gBOIN-ET: Time-to-event generalized Bayesian optimal interval design to accelerate dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Biometrical Journal, 65(7), 2200265. doi:10.1002/bimj.202200265

See also

sim_tite_gboin_et, sim_gboin_et_multi

Examples

# The same toxicity grades with an increasing and with a plateauing
# efficacy
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.94, 0.79, 0.62, 0.50),
  c(0.05, 0.15, 0.20, 0.20),
  c(0.01, 0.05, 0.15, 0.25),
  c(0.00, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05)
)
scenarios <- list(
  "Increasing" = list(
    p_grade = p_grade,
    p_resp_grade = rbind(
      c(0.64, 0.45, 0.20, 0.05),
      c(0.30, 0.40, 0.40, 0.15),
      c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35),
      c(0.01, 0.05, 0.20, 0.45)
    )
  ),
  "Plateau" = list(
    p_grade = p_grade,
    p_resp_grade = rbind(
      c(0.44, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05),
      c(0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.20),
      c(0.15, 0.35, 0.25, 0.25),
      c(0.01, 0.25, 0.50, 0.50)
    )
  )
)
res <- sim_tite_gboin_et_multi(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 1.75 / 3, scenarios = scenarios,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), score_resp = c(0, 0.25, 1, 3),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, window = 30, resp_window = 60,
  accrual_rate = 1 / 10, n_trials = 300, seed = 123
)
res
